newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper shrugs off profit-taking, ends higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper shrugs off profit-taking, ends higher.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly firmer after a choppy, lightly traded session to finish the week a touch higher despite profit-taking, rising LME stocks and an end to the week-long strike at Chile's Quebrada Blanca mine.
The choppy dealings were partly a reflection of the LME cash to three months backwardation dipping some $20 from Thursday's close and widening out again to end at $53/$58, traders said.
"Copper has put in a good performance and firmed during the week," Fred Demler of E D and F Man International said.
July COMEX settled 0.15 cent firmer at 111.60 cents per pound, traded 111.95 to 110.30 cents. Spot May went out 0.05 cent higher at 112.20 cents.
July ended the week 1.35 cents per pound firmer.
LME stocks rose 425 tonnes on Friday, bringing the week's net change to up 4,425 tonnes at 153,350 tonnes.

The market was unmoved by news that striking Chilean Quebrada Blanca copper miners have accepted the company's pay offer and will restart work from the evening shift Friday, according to the mine's general manager James Drake.
Quebrada produces 75,000 tonnes of cathode a year and was operating at half of its capacity by this week, the company said.
